login.title: Sign in
login.tenantHeading: Sign in to the Tenant Portal
login.platformHeading: Sign in to the Platform Console
login.tenantHint: For example: tenant-a — lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
login.tenantInvalid: Invalid tenant ID: 3–32 characters, starting with a letter, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only.
login.platformHint: For platform staff. Signing in always requires a password and a second factor.
login.expired: Your session has expired or was revoked. Please sign in again.

tenantSelect.title: Choose a tenant
tenantSelect.noMemberships: This account is not a member of any active tenant.
tenantSelect.noGrants: No active Support Access Grant. Access to a tenant is only possible through a grant approved by that tenant.

tenant.suspendedBanner: This tenant is suspended: every write is refused, data is read-only.

unavailable.title: Not available yet
unavailable.planned: This screen has not been built yet (task {{task}}). No placeholder figures are shown.
unavailable.postMvp: Post-MVP feature (task {{task}}) — there is no data source yet, so no figures are shown.

notFound.title: Not found
notFound.description: This page or resource does not exist, or you do not have access to it.

forbidden.title: Not allowed
forbidden.description: Your current role is not allowed to view this screen.

stepUp.title: Re-authentication required
stepUp.description: This action is sensitive and requires that you authenticated within the last 15 minutes. Re-authenticate, then repeat the action.

rateLimit.wait_one: Too many requests. Try again in {{count}} second.
rateLimit.wait_other: Too many requests. Try again in {{count}} seconds.

maintenance.banner: The platform is under maintenance. Some features are temporarily unavailable.

problem.unauthenticated: You are not signed in or your session has expired.
problem.reauth_required: Re-authentication is required for this action.
problem.forbidden: You are not allowed to perform this action.
problem.tenant_suspended: This tenant is suspended — writes are refused.
problem.quota_exceeded: The plan's quota has been exceeded.
problem.conflict: Conflicts with the current state — reload and try again.
problem.precondition_failed: The data was changed by someone else — reload and try again.
problem.precondition_required: The data version (If-Match) is missing — reload and try again.
problem.idempotency_key_reuse: The idempotency key was reused with a different request.
problem.rate_limited: Too many requests — wait, then try again.
problem.upstream_rejected: An upstream system refused the request.
problem.instance_unavailable: The tenant's control plane is temporarily not responding.
problem.not_implemented: This function is not implemented on the server yet.
problem.secret_no_longer_available: This credential can no longer be shown: revoke the request and create a new one.

tenantCreate.title: Create tenant
tenantCreate.slugHint: Immutable DNS label: 3–32 characters, lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; starts with a letter, no '--'.
tenantCreate.name: Display name
tenantCreate.ownerEmailHint: Receives the invitation at the tenant configuration step (step 16).
tenantCreate.planHint: Key of an open plan (default: standard). The plan list is on the Plans screen (P4-T03).

drivers.keycloakHint: A realm of its own for the tenant (realm = slug, client mg-portal).
drivers.externalHint: The tenant's issuer and client; the client secret is write-only and never shown again.

tenantCreate.clientSecretHint: Stored in the SecretStore before the job is created; never in the job, audit or any response.
tenantCreate.domainsHint: Optional; comma separated, at most 32 domains.
tenantCreate.reviewNote: Creating the tenant writes the registry (status provisioning) and runs the 19-step tenant.provision job; you will be taken to the job timeline.

errors.name: The name must have 1–128 characters.
errors.issuer: The issuer must be an https URL.

tenantDetail.title: Tenant detail
tenantDetail.suspendDesc: Applies the deny-all policy, refuses every write of the tenant and expires its live pre-auth keys. The instance keeps running. Follow it on the job timeline.
tenantDetail.resumeDesc: Re-applies the desired policy version and reopens writes. Pre-auth keys expired by the suspension are not restored.
tenantDetail.deleteDesc: Deprovisioning: final backup, every node and key expired (point of no return), instance, data and IdP issuer removed; the slug stays reserved.
tenantDetail.deleteTwoPerson: This is a two-person action: a second person (another Super Admin) must approve the request, and both must have authenticated within the last 15 minutes.
tenantDetail.typeSlug: Type the tenant slug to confirm
tenantDetail.skipBackup: Skip the final backup (only when it cannot be taken — the approver sees this flag; the data is kept)
tenantDetail.noPermission: Your role cannot view this section.
tenantDetail.noInstance: The tenant has no instance yet.
tenantDetail.noRelay: The tenant has no relay region yet.
tenantDetail.unmeasured: Figures without a source (no made-up numbers)

job.title: Job
job.tenantCreated: The tenant is in the registry (provisioning). The 19-step progress is below and updates itself.
job.settled: The job is in a final state — no longer updating.
job.polling: Updating automatically (every 2 seconds, 5 seconds after the first minute).
job.noSteps: The job has not recorded any step yet.

control.cancelDesc: A job that has not started is cancelled at once; a running one stops after its current step and waits for a retry or a rollback.
control.retryDesc: Resumes from the failed step (finished steps are skipped); a rolled-back tenant.provision starts a new job from step 3.
control.rollbackDesc: Runs the compensation of the finished steps in reverse order. Past the point of no return the server refuses — only a retry is left.

approvals.title: Pending approvals (2P)
approvals.intro: Two-person actions of the platform. The approver must differ from the requester, hold the action's own permission and have authenticated within the last 15 minutes.
approvals.caption: Approval requests

approval.title: Approval request
approval.requestedNotice: The request was created. A second person must approve it before the action runs.
approval.payloadIntro: Exactly the parameters that run once approved — nothing else. The hash the browser computes from the payload shown must match the server's.
approval.hashUnverifiable: The payload cannot be verified in the browser — approval is not possible
approval.hashMismatch: Hashes do NOT match — do not approve
approval.closed: The request is {{status}} — it can no longer be decided.
approval.selfRequest: You made this request: a second person must approve or reject it.
approval.notPermitted: Your role cannot decide this action.
approval.stepUpNote: Approving or rejecting requires an authentication within the last 15 minutes; otherwise you will be asked to sign in again.
approval.approveDesc: The action runs right after the approval, with exactly the payload whose hash is below.
approval.rejectDesc: The request is closed; the requester has to make a new one if needed.
approval.typeSlug: Type the slug of the tenant to delete

instance.title: Instance detail
instance.noConfig: The instance has no configuration version recorded by the orchestrator (adopted instance) — reconfigure/upgrade will be refused (409).
instance.restartDesc: Controlled restart: Host Agent start guard, health gate, post-start policy check. The tenant's clients briefly lose the control plane. Follow it on the job timeline.
instance.backupDesc: Creates an instance.backup job (VACUUM INTO while running, cold copy when stopped); the backup is encrypted and its signed manifest verified before it succeeds.
instance.reconfigureDesc: Renders a new configuration version from the one in effect plus the changes below, configtest, write, restart and health gate; a failure rolls back to the previous version. Leave empty to keep.
instance.nameserversHint: 1–8 addresses, separated by commas or spaces.
instance.upgradeDesc: Preflight (allowed version, configtest of the target), cold backup, image swap, health gate, contract smoke; a failure after the swap restores the backup on the old image. The digest must be in the Host Agent's allowlist.
instance.restoreDesc: Restores the tenant's Headscale from a backup: every API key/pre-auth key of the backup stops working, nodes revoked after the backup are expired again.
instance.twoPerson: This is a two-person action: a second person approves it in the approval queue; both must have authenticated within 15 minutes.
instance.olderRestorePoint: PostgreSQL was restored to a point OLDER than this backup
instance.olderRestorePointHint: Keeps the backup's policy as a version to review and flags the tenant for Owner review.
instance.quarantineDesc: Isolates a suspected compromised instance now: edge detached (the tenant hostname answers 404), container stopped (data and logs kept), Critical security event. Only a two-person request lifts it.
instance.typeHostname: Type the control hostname to confirm
instance.releaseDesc: Once approved: the Host Agent starts it through the start guard, the applied policy is checked, the edge is attached again; any failure isolates it again.

errors.nodeExpiry: Node expiry must be an integer 1–3650.
errors.derpRegion: DERP region must be an integer 900–999.
errors.digest: The digest must look like sha256:<64 lowercase hex characters>.
errors.sameDigest: The instance already runs this image.

host.title: Host detail
host.noEntry: No public IPv4 yet (placement skips this host)

relayRegions.readOnly: Read-only in the MVP: the embedded relay (DERP) follows each tenant's instance; adding/changing regions is Phase 7.

settings.intro: Closed key set: only the keys below exist. Changes need a Super Admin who authenticated within 15 minutes; each change is audited (before/after).
settings.readOnlyRole: Your role can only view the settings.

desc.approval_ttl_hours: Lifetime of a new approval request (hours, 1–168).
desc.quota_max_tenants: Maximum number of tenants not deleted or failed (tenant creation quota).
desc.maintenance: Persistent maintenance flag — written by host commands only.

settings.editDesc: The new value applies at the next read by the component using this key. If someone else just changed it, you will see the latest value before deciding again.
settings.useLatest: Use the latest version and edit again

users.intro: Platform roles assigned here are always below Super Admin; granting or revoking Super Admin always needs another Super Admin's approval (two-person). Nobody edits their own entry.
users.createDesc: The person needs an account at the platform IdP first; the first login matches by sub, never by email. Requires authentication within 15 minutes.
users.subject: Subject (sub) at the platform IdP
users.roleHint: Super Admin cannot be assigned here (use the two-person request).
users.editDesc: Changing the role or disabling revokes every session of that person at once.
users.disableDesc: Revokes every session of that person; the record is kept for audit, re-enable with Edit → Active.
users.grantDesc: Super Admin holds every platform permission, including roles and IdPs. Once approved, every session of that person is revoked.
users.revokeDesc: The last Super Admin cannot be removed. Once approved, every session of that person is revoked.
users.twoPerson: Two-person action: another Super Admin approves it in the approval queue; both must have authenticated within 15 minutes.

idps.intro: Issuer, client ID and driver are immutable; only the claim constraints can change. A tenant's IdP: a change needs a second Super Admin's approval, is written to the tenant's audit and notifies the Tenant Owners.

idp.title: Identity provider
idp.immutable: Issuer, client ID, driver and scope cannot change (§8.2) — switching IdP is a separate migration.
idp.requiredClaimsHint: An object of up to 16 claims; values are a string/number/boolean or an array of accepted values. sub, iss, aud are not allowed.
idp.domainsHint: Up to 32 domains, separated by commas or new lines.
idp.editDesc: Only changed fields are sent. Requires authentication within 15 minutes.
idp.tenantTwoPerson: A tenant's IdP: the change creates an approval request (second Super Admin) and does NOT apply until approved; the Tenant Owners are notified and the tenant's audit records it.

errors.mapping: Claim names use letters, digits, _ . : / - only (up to 128).
errors.domains: A domain is invalid or there are more than 32.

plans.intro: A plan key is immutable; every plan holds the four quota limits. A closed plan takes no new tenant, tenants on it keep it. New limits apply at the next quota check.
plans.createDesc: The four quota limits are required; leave other fields empty for no such limit.
plans.editDesc: The limits sent replace the plan's whole limits document.
plans.keyHint: Lowercase letters, digits, _ or -, starting with a letter (up to 63).
plans.name: Plan name
plans.activeHint: Closing a plan does not affect tenants on it.

tenantEdit.title: Edit tenant {{slug}}
tenantEdit.desc: Change the name, plan or limit overrides. Lowering a limit below current use deletes nothing — it only blocks the next addition.
tenantEdit.overrideHint: The API only returns effective limits (plan + overrides): the values sent replace every existing override; leaving every field empty removes all overrides.

ui.readOnlyActions: The tenant is read-only: changes are disabled.
ui.copyFailed: Could not copy — select the text and copy it manually.

kinds.tenant_suspended: Tenant {{tenant}} has been suspended — data is read-only.
kinds.tenant_deleted: Tenant {{tenant}} was deleted; its data keys will be destroyed after {{keys_destroy_after}}.
kinds.device_expiring: Device {{device_name}} expires at {{expires_at}} — it must re-authenticate.
kinds.support_grant_requested: Platform staff {{staff}} requests a Support Access Grant — the tenant must decide.
kinds.support_break_glass: Break-glass: {{staff}} was granted emergency support access (approved by {{approver}}).
kinds.support_grant_used: Platform staff {{staff}} acted in the tenant through a Support Access Grant.
kinds.approval_requested: A new approval request is waiting: {{action}}.
kinds.idp_admin_change: Administrative change at the Identity Provider: {{action}} (by {{actor}}).
kinds.instance_restored: The tenant's control plane was restored from the backup of {{backup_created_at}}.
kinds.enrollment_approved: Your device request ({{device_label}}) was approved — choose Start before {{expires_at}}.
kinds.enrollment_approved_support: Your device request ({{device_label}}) was approved by platform support staff (through the support access grant of the tenant) — choose Start before {{expires_at}}.
kinds.enrollment_rejected_support: Your device request ({{device_label}}) was rejected by platform support staff (through the support access grant of the tenant).

dashboard.onlineNote: Online as seen by the control plane at the last sync — not a measurement of the network path.

reasons.never_synced: The device inventory has never been synced — no figures yet.
reasons.no_source: The platform has no data source for this section yet.
reasons.not_served: A source exists but the overview does not serve this figure yet.

reason.circuit_open: Calls to the instance paused after repeated failures.
reason.api_key_rejected: The platform's API key was rejected.
reason.edge_rejected: The edge refused the administrative call.
reason.not_located: The tenant's instance could not be located.
reason.stale: The last check result is stale.
reason.no_probe: No probe exists for this component yet.

devices.noOsNote: Operating system, client version and endpoints are not shown: the Headscale API does not provide them (HS-14).
devices.tagInvalid: A tag looks like tag:<name> (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens).

review.title: Review of tagged nodes that never expire
review.description: Tagged nodes never expire and have no owner (HS-19, PL-09) — review them periodically (quarterly) and revoke the ones no longer used (§7.4, ADR-23).
review.empty: No tagged node that never expires.

explain.pending: The {{kind}} was accepted — waiting for Headscale to confirm (read-back). The device is NOT revoked until the state is "applied".
explain.applied: The {{kind}} is applied: Headscale confirmed it on read-back.
explain.failed: The {{kind}} failed: Headscale refused or the retries ran out. The device may still have access — try again.

deleted.title: Device deleted
deleted.description: Headscale confirmed the deletion: the device is no longer in the inventory.

detail.manageRoutes: Review and approve routes on the Routes screen

rename.title: Rename
rename.label: Name in the tailnet (DNS label)
rename.hint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; 1–63 characters; no leading or trailing hyphen.

revoke.title: Revocation
revoke.description: Revocation has two phases: the request is recorded at once, and it is "applied" only once Headscale confirms it.
revoke.confirmExpire: The device's key expires now: it loses tailnet access until it signs in again.
revoke.confirmDelete: The device is removed from the tailnet and from the inventory. Using it again requires a new registration.
revoke.twoPhase: This page follows the request until Headscale confirms it.

relay.intro: The tenant's DERP relays: the assigned regions and the platform's latest probe.
relay.empty: No relay is assigned to this tenant yet.

reasons.unsupported: The component does not provide this figure (the embedded DERP exports no relay metrics).
reasons.no_source: The platform has no source for this figure yet.

healthReason.relay_unreachable: The relay is unreachable (DERP and STUN).
healthReason.stale: The last probe result is stale.
healthReason.no_probe: This kind of region is not probed yet.

users.empty: The tenant has no members yet.

user.profileFromIdp: Name and email come from the IdP at every sign-in — not edited here.
user.ruleNoActions: You cannot act on this member: only roles strictly below yours (rule 3a — a Tenant Admin does not lock, offboard or change the role of an Owner or another Admin).
user.selfNoActions: This is your own account: you do not lock, offboard or change your own role here.

access.title: Portal access
access.description: Locking blocks Portal sign-in and revokes every session (reversible); devices stay on the network — offboarding cuts them off.
access.lockDesc: The person is signed out at once and cannot sign in to the Portal until unlocked. Nodes and pre-auth keys are not touched.
access.unlockDesc: The person can sign in again if the IdP still allows it.
access.sessionsDesc: Every Portal session of the person ends at once; they can sign in again if the membership and the IdP allow it.

role.title: Role
role.description: Only the roles you may give under rule 3a are listed. The Owner role is only given by an ownership transfer.
role.sessionsNote: Every session of the person is revoked (their rights change).
role.adminHint: A change touching the Tenant Admin role or an Owner is made by an Owner only and needs a recent sign-in (step-up).

owner.title: Transfer ownership
owner.description: Give the Tenant Owner role to this member. By default you become a Tenant Admin.
owner.confirmDesc: This person becomes a Tenant Owner. The sessions of both of you are revoked — you will have to sign in again.
owner.typeLabel: Type the recipient's email (or name) to confirm
owner.keep: I keep the Owner role (two Owners)

offboard.title: Offboard
offboard.description: Ends access for good: revokes sessions, leaves every group, expires every node and pre-auth key, disables the account at a platform-hosted IdP.

effects.sessions: At once: the membership becomes offboarded, every Portal session is revoked, the identity is disabled.
effects.groups: At once: leaves every group (the policy is applied again).
effects.nodes: Job member.offboard: expires every node and pre-auth key of the person, then reads them back to verify.
effects.idp: Job member.offboard: disables the account at a platform-hosted IdP (a tenant's own IdP: not applicable).

offboard.final: Offboarded is final — it cannot be reactivated here.
offboard.typeLabel: Type the member's email (or name) to confirm
offboard.retryDescription: The offboarding job ended in error: nodes or pre-auth keys may still be valid. Running it again creates a new job.

explain.pending: Phase 2 is running — nodes and pre-auth keys are NOT known to be expired until the job has verified them.
explain.applied: Applied and verified: nodes and pre-auth keys have expired; the account at a platform-hosted IdP is disabled.
explain.failed: The job ended in error — nodes or keys may still be valid. Offboard again to create a new job.

invite.title: Invite a member
invite.description: The invited person signs in for the first time through the tenant's IdP with this exact (verified) email and gets the chosen role.
invite.roleHint: Only the roles you may invite are listed (below your own — rule 3a).
invite.hoursInvalid: The lifetime is a whole number from 1 to 720.

invitations.intro: Invitations of people who never signed in. With a platform-hosted IdP, the job member.idp_invite creates (or finds) the account and emails its setup.
invitations.watching: Invitation sent — its IdP status (job member.idp_invite) updates in the table.
invitations.resendDesc: The invitation gets a new link and lifetime (7 days); the old link stops working.
invitations.revokeDesc: The link in the invitation email no longer works.

groups.intro: Groups are compiled into the policy as group:<name>. A member change applies the policy again (job policy.apply).
groups.name: Name
groups.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; starts with a letter; at most 50 characters.
groups.sensitiveExplain: Sensitive group: a member change needs another Owner/Admin to approve (the flag is set in the Tenant Owner's security settings).
groups.sensitiveEditNote: Sensitive group: saving does NOT change anything now but creates an approval request (needs a recent sign-in); the set applies once a second person approves.
groups.onlyActive: Only active members can be added to a group.
groups.tooMany: At most {{max}} members in one save.
groups.staleReloaded: Someone else just changed the group — the new version was loaded; check it and save again.
groups.renameNote: Renaming changes group:<name> in the policy — the policy is applied again.
groups.deleteDesc: A group still named as the owner of a network resource cannot be deleted.
groups.deleteSensitive: A sensitive group with members cannot be deleted — remove its members through an approval first.
groups.deleteConfirmDesc_one: {{count}} member leaves the group; the policy is applied again.
groups.deleteConfirmDesc_other: {{count}} members leave the group; the policy is applied again.
groups.typeName: Type the group name to confirm

explain.pending: An approval request was created — the members have NOT changed. Another Owner/Admin must approve it.
explain.executed: Approved and applied with exactly the proposed members.
explain.rejected: The request was rejected — the members did not change.
explain.expired: The request expired — the members did not change.

policies.intro: Policies are written on a typed model (members, groups, tags and resources chosen by id), checked by lint L1–L13 and CheckPolicy on the instance, and reviewed before they are applied. Groups, hosts and tagOwners are rendered from the tenant's tables when a version is applied.
policies.noVersions: The tenant has no policy version yet.

editor.noResources: The network resource catalog has no read API yet (P4-T12): only resources already referenced can be chosen; use the HuJSON mode with the alias name.
editor.denyAll: No rule: this policy blocks every connection (deny-all).
editor.sshHint: None by default. accept always allows port forwarding and is not recorded (L10 — needs an acknowledgement); check is refused.
editor.appHint: Shown read-only in the form — edit them in the HuJSON mode.
editor.autoApproversHint: None by default. Only the platform's router/exit tags need no acknowledgement (L7); autoApprovers run again on every apply.

ack.title: Rule acknowledgements
ack.hint: A rule that needs an acknowledgement passes validation only with one and a reason (≥ 5 characters). Acknowledgements are not part of the HuJSON text.

desc.L4: * or a default route as a destination (subnet routes and exit nodes included).
desc.L7: autogroup:internet without via, or autoApprovers other than platform tags.
desc.L10: an SSH accept rule (port forwarding always on).
desc.L12: tagOwners with owners (the platform always renders empty owners).
desc.L13: autogroup:member when the tenant uses the headscale_oidc identity mode.

ack.reasonHint: 5–500 characters; stored in the version's content and shown to the reviewer.

report.title: Validation result
report.none: This version has not been validated.
report.stale: This report is about an older revision — validate again.
report.testsNote: Tests are generated at validation/application (see below); impact checks also rely on CheckPolicy and the diff — not a simulation of effective access.

finding.wildcard_destination: * or a default route as a destination — blocked unless a Tenant Owner acknowledges it with a reason (L4).
finding.danger_all_source: autogroup:danger-all as a source — always blocked (L5).
finding.undeclared_group: The group referenced does not exist in the tenant (L6).
finding.undeclared_tag: The tag is not in the tenant's tag catalog (L6).
finding.undeclared_user: The member does not exist, is offboarded, or the e-mail belongs to no member (L6).
finding.undeclared_resource: No network resource has this name (alias) (L6).
finding.unresolved_reference: The reference no longer exists in the tenant — fix it before saving.
finding.ambiguous_user: Several members have this e-mail — write the member as mg-<membership>@.
finding.ambiguous_resource: Several network resources have this name.
finding.internet_without_via: autogroup:internet without a via tag (exit node) — needs an L7 acknowledgement.
finding.auto_approver_not_platform: autoApprovers other than the platform's router/exit tags — needs an L7 acknowledgement.
finding.ssh_accept: SSH accept always allows port forwarding and is not recorded — needs an L10 acknowledgement.
finding.self_large_tenant: autogroup:self in a large tenant costs on every change (L8).
finding.member_oidc: autogroup:member in headscale_oidc mode includes every user of the IdP — needs an L13 acknowledgement.
finding.user_token: A user token of the output is not mg-<membership>@ (L11).
finding.missing_grants: No grants key — Headscale would allow all traffic (L1). Use "grants": [] for deny-all.
finding.null_grants: "grants": null means allow-all (L1) — use an explicit array.
finding.empty: The policy text is empty — Headscale would store it and allow all traffic at its next start (L2). Not sent.
finding.managed_key: This key is rendered from the tenant's tables (groups, resources, tag catalog) — remove it from the text and manage it on its page (L3).
finding.acls_unsupported: acls is the legacy format — write the rules as grants (L3).
finding.node_attrs: nodeAttrs is refused in the MVP (L3, HS-22).
finding.tests_generated: tests/sshTests are generated at apply time, not written by hand (L3).
finding.unsupported_key: This key is not part of a tenant policy (L3).
finding.misspelled_key: The key's case is wrong — Headscale matches keys case-insensitively, so it is refused.
finding.comment_key: A key starting with # is silently ignored by Headscale — refused.
finding.null_value: null is not allowed here (it could hide a rule).
finding.invalid_cidr: The prefix has host bits set.
finding.invalid_prefix: A route must be a masked IP prefix.
finding.via_not_asserted: Generated tests cannot assert the access through via of this rule (V-24).
finding.self_not_asserted: Generated tests cannot assert the access to autogroup:self of this rule (V-24).
finding.tests_failed: Headscale refused the generated tests: an assertion is wrong, or a device they name is gone (PL-04).

hujson.label: HuJSON text
hujson.hint: Comments and trailing commas are allowed. Members by e-mail or mg-<membership>@; group: and tag: by name; resources by alias. Changes take effect only after "Translate to form" and save.
hujson.readOnlyHint: Read-only — this version cannot be edited.
hujson.failed_one: Could not translate: {{count}} error. The form is unchanged.
hujson.failed_other: Could not translate: {{count}} errors. The form is unchanged.
hujson.imported: Translated into the form — review it, then save.

diff.title: Diff
diff.blocking: This version's validation report has blocking errors.
diff.omitted: The document is too large: line diff omitted (the grants diff is still there).
diff.lines: Line diff of the rendered policy
diff.note: Both sides are rendered over the current tables ({{from}} → {{to}}).

current.title: Current state
current.convergedUnknown: Not observable from Headscale — each client receives the new policy at its next update (T-18).
current.stepUp: Apply/rollback need a sign-in within 15 minutes

job.title: policy.apply job
job.succeeded: Applied: Headscale holds exactly the policy sent (read-back sha256 matches).

stale.title: The version changed elsewhere (412)
stale.body: The copy you are looking at is outdated (another revision). Reload the latest one and try again — unsaved changes are discarded.

actions.title: Lifecycle
actions.saveFirst: There are unsaved changes — save before validating or reviewing.
actions.fourEyesSelf: 4-eyes is on: you wrote or submitted this version, so you cannot approve it — another Owner/Admin approves it.
actions.ownerOnly: The version acknowledges a rule only a Tenant Owner may accept (L4/L12) — a Tenant Owner approves it.

staleBase.title: Stale base (409 stale_base)
staleBase.body: This version was written on an older desired version; the desired version has changed since. Create a new draft from this content (based on the current desired version), validate and review it again.

content.title: Content
content.platformText: A platform version (HuJSON text, no typed model) — read-only.
content.backToDraft: Saving returns the version to draft and clears its approval and validation result.

approve.title: Approve version {{n}}?
approve.peer: You approve as the second person (4-eyes). The approval is bound to the exact content you reviewed.
approve.self: 4-eyes is off: you confirm the diff and the validation result of the rendered policy yourself (review_mode = self).
approve.reviewed: I have reviewed the diff and the validation result of this version.

reject.title: Reject version {{n}}?
reject.description: The version becomes rejected; its author can create a new draft.

rollback.title: Roll back to the content of version {{n}}?
rollback.description: Creates a new version with this content (its approval is inherited — the content was approved before), makes it desired and applies it at once (policy.apply job).

apply.title: Apply version {{n}}?
apply.description: The version becomes desired and the policy.apply job renders it over the current tables → lint → CheckPolicy → SetPolicy → read-back sha256.
apply.stepUp: This needs a sign-in within the last 15 minutes (step-up) — when asked, sign in again and retry.
apply.converged: "Applied to Headscale" does not mean every client has the new policy.

templates.title: Least-privilege templates
templates.intro: Templates are platform data (versioned): the server renders one deterministically into typed rules (by id) that are added to the draft — not saved, not applied. Save, validate and review as any change.
templates.applied: {{count}} rule(s) from “{{name}}” ({{version}}) added to the draft — save to keep them.
templates.replaced: The draft was replaced by “{{name}}” ({{version}}) — save to keep it.
templates.reportTitle: Check of the template's rules on their own

params.tag_id: Tag of the router / exit node (via)
params.portsHint: Comma separated, e.g. tcp:22, tcp:443. * is not accepted (least privilege).
params.noResources: The network resource catalog cannot be read (the role cannot read it, or there is none yet).

deny-all.name: Baseline deny-all
deny-all.description: Removes every rule: grants: [] — denies every connection (like the baseline policy of a new tenant).

own-devices.name: Only my own devices
own-devices.description: Every member reaches their own devices (autogroup:member → autogroup:self) on the chosen ports.

group-to-resource.name: Group → resource by port
group-to-resource.description: A group reaches one network resource, on the chosen ports only.

admins-to-devices.name: Admins → every device over management ports
admins-to-devices.description: An admin group reaches every device (members' and tagged) on management ports only (tcp:22 by default).

exit-node.name: Exit node through a via tag
exit-node.description: A group uses the Internet through the exit node carrying the chosen tag (autogroup:internet with via).

subnet-router.name: Subnet router by resource
subnet-router.description: A group reaches one resource (subnet) through the router carrying the chosen tag (via), on the chosen ports.

notes.tests_self_not_asserted: Generated tests CANNOT assert access to autogroup:self: Headscale runs tests on its global filter, which leaves self rules out (V-24). Check with real connections.
notes.tests_via_not_asserted: Generated tests CANNOT assert access through via: Headscale runs tests on its global filter, which leaves via rules out (V-24). Check with real connections.
notes.routes_need_approval: The routes of the router/exit node still have to be approved on the Routes page.
notes.self_large_tenant: autogroup:self is costly in a large tenant (L8).
notes.replaces_draft: Replaces every rule of the draft.

testsGen.title: Generated tests
testsGen.intro: At every validation/application the server generates tests from the grants and the devices of the moment; Headscale runs them on CheckPolicy/SetPolicy and refuses the policy when an assertion is wrong. Tests only see the global filter: they CANNOT assert access from via or autogroup:self (V-24) — this is not a simulation of effective access.

skipped.via_not_assertable: has via — tests cannot see it (V-24)
skipped.self_not_assertable: destination is only autogroup:self — tests cannot see it (V-24)
skipped.no_testable_port: no port tests can check (only * or a protocol tests do not take)
skipped.no_source_device: no source has a device yet (PL-04)
skipped.no_destination: no destination resolves to an address yet (PL-04)

tags.intro: The tenant's tag catalog: only tags listed here can be set on devices, enrollment keys or used in a policy. Every tag is rendered into tagOwners with no owner — only the platform sets tags. Every catalog change applies the policy again.
tags.deleteDescription: A tag still referenced by devices, enrollment keys, network resources or policies cannot be deleted (409, with the counts).
tags.inUse: The tag is still referenced — remove the references (devices, keys, resources, policy versions) and delete it again.
tags.nameHint: tag:<lowercase letters, digits, hyphens>, at most 54 characters; cannot be changed later.
tags.stale: The tag was changed elsewhere — close the dialog and open it again to edit the latest copy.

audit.tenantIntro: Administrative actions in this tenant, newest first — including actions of platform staff under a Support Access Grant (actor type “Platform support”).
audit.platformIntro: Platform events: actions of platform staff (including support access requests, break-glass and revocations), their denials and platform-level system events.
audit.actionInvalid: A dotted lowercase action, e.g. device.rename.
audit.caption: Audit events

support.tenantIntro: Platform staff can enter this tenant only through a time-boxed grant (at most 8 hours) that you approve here. Every action they take appears in the audit log. You can revoke a grant at any time — it stops at their next request.
support.platformIntro: Support access to a tenant needs a grant: the tenant approves it in its Portal; if the tenant cannot be reached, a second Super Admin may approve it as break-glass (high security event, every Tenant Owner is notified).
support.viewActions: See the actions of platform support in the audit log
support.caption: Support access grants
support.adminBreakglassOnly: The Support Admin role is granted only through break-glass by two Super Admins.
support.requestIntro: The grant starts pending; it gives access only once the tenant (or, in an emergency, a second Super Admin) approves it. The window starts now.
support.chooseTenant: Choose an active or suspended tenant
support.requested: Request sent — waiting for the tenant's decision.
support.typeSlug: Type the tenant slug to confirm

confirm.approveDesc: {{staff}} will be able to act in this tenant as {{role}} until the end of the window. Requires a recent sign-in.
confirm.rejectDesc: {{staff}} will not get access ({{role}}). A rejected request is final.
confirm.revokeDesc: {{staff}} loses access ({{role}}) at the next request.
confirm.breakglassDesc: You are the second Super Admin approving access of {{staff}} to tenant {{tenant}} without the tenant's decision. A high-severity security event is raised and every Tenant Owner is notified.

support.grantEnded: Your Support Access Grant for this tenant may have expired or been revoked — the action was not performed.

approvals.intro: Changes inside the tenant that need a second person (turning off 4-eyes, removing a sensitive group, members of a sensitive group…). The requester cannot approve their own request.
approvals.caption: Approval requests of the tenant
approvals.requestedNotice: Your change is not in effect yet: another Owner or Admin must approve it.
approvals.payloadIntro: The exact payload stored with the request. Your browser recomputes its SHA-256; you can approve only when it matches.
approvals.hashMismatch: Payload hash does not match — do not approve
approvals.selfRequest: You made this request — another person must decide it.
approvals.notPermitted: Your role cannot decide approval requests.
approvals.approveDesc: The change is executed immediately after your approval. Requires a recent sign-in.

settings.intro: Settings of this tenant. Security settings can only be changed by a Tenant Owner; lifting a two-person control needs the approval of another Owner or Admin.
settings.newDevice: Notify Owners and Admins when a new device joins
settings.policyApplied: Notify Owners and Admins when a policy is applied
settings.preauthTtlHint: <n>m or <n>h, between 5 minutes and 90 days; empty = the platform limit.
settings.readOnlyNote: Your role can only read these settings.
settings.securityIntro: Turning off 4-eyes or removing a sensitive group does not take effect immediately: it becomes an approval request for another Owner or Admin.

identityModes.headscale_oidc: Headscale OIDC (not available in this version)

settings.self_enroll: Allow end users to enroll their own devices
settings.nodeExpiryHint: 0 = never, <n>d or <n>h (at most 3650 days); empty = default.
settings.securityReadOnly: Only a Tenant Owner can change the security settings.
settings.approvalNotInEffect: The change is NOT in effect yet: another Owner or Admin must approve it.

idp.intro: The identity provider members of this tenant sign in with. Issuer and client ID never change here (changing the provider is a migration).
idp.immutableNote: Issuer, client ID and type are immutable.
idp.domainsHint: One domain per line; empty = any domain.
idp.mappingInvalid: Enter a JSON object whose values are non-empty strings.
idp.secretHint: 16–512 characters; leave empty to keep the current secret. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
idp.stepUpNote: Requires a recent sign-in (step-up). Changes apply at the next sign-in.
idp.readOnlyNote: Only a Tenant Owner can change the identity provider.

job.inProgress: Applying — not in effect until the job succeeds.
job.failed: The job did not succeed — the change was not applied.

approval.title: Approval request created — nothing has changed yet
approval.description: This tenant requires two-person control (4-eyes) for routes: a second person who may approve routes and decide approvals must approve this request. The routes are approved in Headscale only once the request is approved.
approval.sendId: Send the request ID to the approver (another Owner/Admin of the tenant).

explain.pending: The change is NOT in effect yet: waiting for a second person to approve it.
explain.approved: Approved, being executed — the routes do not change until it completes.
explain.executed: Approved and executed: the routes are approved in Headscale.
explain.rejected: The request was rejected — the routes did not change.
explain.expired: The request expired — the routes did not change.

fieldErrors.value_not_in_tailnet: The value must be the tailnet address of one of the tenant's devices or lie inside an approved subnet route.
fieldErrors.type_mismatch: An A record needs an IPv4 address, an AAAA record an IPv6 address.
fieldErrors.invalid_value: The value must be a unicast IP address.
fieldErrors.name_platform_domain: A name under the platform's domain is accepted only inside the tenant's MagicDNS domain.
fieldErrors.ports_with_icmp: The icmp protocol has no ports.
fieldErrors.service_needs_ports: A service resource must declare at least one port.
fieldErrors.subnet_prefix: A subnet must be a prefix (shorter than one address, longer than /0).
fieldErrors.address_not_canonical: The prefix must have no host bits set (e.g. 10.0.0.0/24).
fieldErrors.single_address: A host or a service has exactly one address.
fieldErrors.unknown_group: The owner group must be a group of the tenant.
fieldErrors.invalid_group: The owner group must be a group of the tenant.

routes.intro: Advertised and approved routes of the router devices, from the device register (each row with its sync time). Advertised routes that are not approved are not distributed to any client (double opt-in).
routes.empty: No device advertises or has approved routes yet.

warnings.untagged_router: The device is a user's node (not a tagged node): the route would depend on a personal device (T-08).
warnings.exit_node: The device is an exit node: clients' Internet traffic goes through it.

dialog.approveDesc: Approved routes are distributed by Headscale: clients allowed by the policy reach these networks through the device.
dialog.exitRisk: Risk: all Internet traffic of the clients that pick this exit node goes through the device.
dialog.exitRiskDetail: The device (and whoever administers it) can see and tamper with that traffic. Approve only devices your organisation manages (tagged nodes), hardened and monitored.
dialog.exitAck: I understand the risk and want to approve the exit node (0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0).
dialog.revokeDesc: The device stops routing the selected prefixes: clients lose their path to those networks through this device.
dialog.stale: The device's routes changed: fresh data was loaded — check your selection and confirm again.

dns.noNameservers: None yet (the instance has no configuration version written by the orchestrator).
dns.pending: An instance reconfiguration has not finished yet:
dns.applied: Applied — the instance runs with the new nameservers.
dns.nsLabel: Nameservers (1–{{max}} IP addresses, one per line)
dns.nsHint: Unicast IPv4 or IPv6 addresses; no duplicates.
dns.confirmRestart: The tenant's Headscale instance will restart in a controlled way (behind a health gate, rolling back to the previous configuration if it does not come up).
dns.confirmRelay: During the restart the tenant's relay (DERP) sessions are dropped and clients reconnect.
dns.stale: The DNS settings changed since you opened the page: fresh data was loaded — check, then confirm again.
dns.recordsIntro: A/AAAA records resolved inside the tailnet. A record must point to the tailnet address of one of the tenant's devices or to an IP inside an approved subnet route. Adding or deleting does not restart the instance.
dns.recordWritten: Records file written — Headscale reloads it without a restart.
dns.deleteDesc: The name will no longer resolve to {{value}} once the records file is written again.
dns.nameHint: Lowercase FQDN, at least 2 labels, no wildcard; under the platform's domain only inside {{domain}}.
dns.nameHintGeneric: Lowercase FQDN, at least 2 labels, no wildcard.
dns.valueHint: A device's tailnet IP, or an IP inside an approved subnet route.

resources.intro: The network resource catalog: each resource is an alias (hosts key) the policy can refer to. Every change re-renders and re-applies the policy (policy.apply job).
resources.deleteDesc: The alias leaves the catalog and the policy is applied again; rules referring to this alias must be changed first.
resources.stale: The resource was changed by someone else: the list was reloaded — open it again and redo the change.
resources.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter (≤ 63 characters); unique in the tenant.
resources.addressHintSubnet: A prefix without host bits, e.g. 10.0.0.0/24.
resources.portsHint: Ports or ranges separated by commas: 443, 8000-8100. Empty = all ports (a service needs ports; icmp has none).
resources.policyNote: After saving, the policy is applied again in the background (policy.apply job).

enroll.intro: Add your device to the tenant's network with the official Tailscale client. Personal devices with a browser use web-auth (there is no key to copy); servers, containers, CI and phones use a single-use pre-auth key.

decider.supportApproved: Approved by platform support staff (support access grant)
decider.supportRejected: Rejected by platform support staff (support access grant)

enroll.selfEnrollHint: The tenant may not let users add their own devices — contact the tenant's administrator.

linux.name: Linux
linux.step1: Install the official Tailscale client from the distribution's package repository (pkgs.tailscale.com).
linux.step2: Create a device request on this page and keep it open in this same browser (same session).
linux.step3: Run the command shown here with sudo; it prints a sign-in link — open it and confirm in the Portal.

windows.name: Windows
windows.step1: Install the official Tailscale client for Windows (MSI from Tailscale's download page) — the tenant's LoginURL can be preset at install time (below).
windows.step2: Create a device request on this page and keep it open in this same browser (same session).
windows.step3: Run the command shown here in an elevated PowerShell; open the sign-in link it prints and confirm in the Portal.

macos.name: macOS
macos.step1: Install the official Tailscale client for macOS (standalone package or App Store).
macos.step2: Create a device request on this page and keep it open in this same browser (same session).
macos.step3: Run the command shown here in Terminal; open the sign-in link it prints and confirm in the Portal.

ios.name: iOS
ios.step1: Install the official Tailscale app from the App Store.
ios.step2: Mobile clients cannot choose their hostname: use a single-use pre-auth key from the Portal (key method below).
ios.step3: In the app, choose a custom coordination server (Settings → Accounts → Use a custom coordination server), enter the login server shown here and the key.

android.name: Android
android.step1: Install the official Tailscale app from Google Play.
android.step2: Mobile clients cannot choose their hostname: use a single-use pre-auth key from the Portal (key method below).
android.step3: In the app, choose an alternate server (Accounts → Use an alternate server), enter the login server shown here and the key.

enroll.privacy: The official Tailscale client may send diagnostic logs to Tailscale Inc. before it first connects to this network. Managed installations should set TS_NO_LOGS_NO_SUPPORT=true (or pass --no-logs-no-support).

instructions.noInstance: The tenant has no running control plane yet — devices cannot be added. Try again later or contact an administrator.
instructions.windowsMsi: Install the MSI with the tenant's LoginURL
instructions.windowsPolicy: Or set the LoginURL system policy (already installed)
instructions.mobileNote: Web-auth does not work on phones (they cannot use the hostname that carries the enrollment code) — use a single-use pre-auth key.

wizard.title: Enroll a new device
wizard.webHint: Default for personal devices: run the command, open the link the client prints in this browser and confirm. No key to copy.
wizard.webOff: The tenant turned web-auth off — use a pre-auth key.
wizard.keyHint: For servers, containers, CI or devices without a browser: single-use, short-lived, shown once.
wizard.label: Device label (optional)
wizard.labelHint: Device name after enrollment: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens (up to 63 characters).
wizard.labelInvalid: Use lowercase a–z, digits and hyphens only, not starting or ending with a hyphen.
wizard.ttlHint: 1 to {{max}} minutes (the tenant may set a lower cap).
wizard.noRequest: Your role can read instructions and requests but cannot request a device.

pendingApproval.title: Request sent — awaiting approval
pendingApproval.body: The tenant requires an approval before a command or key is issued. Once approved, come back to Add device and use the button in your requests (within 24 hours).

issued.title: Device request: {{label}}
issued.runCommand: Run this command on the device (once, bound to this Portal session):
issued.next1: Run the command as is on your device — do not change the hostname.
issued.next2: The client prints a sign-in link: open it in THIS browser; the Portal shows the confirmation page.
issued.next3: If the link opens in another browser, paste it into "Paste a link or Auth ID" below.

ended.expired: The command expired — create a new request.

key.onceWarning: The key is shown ONCE and is not stored by the platform. Copy it to a safe place now; closing this dialog loses it (revoke and issue a new key).
key.envHint: Put the key in the TS_AUTHKEY environment variable before running the command — do not paste it on the command line, so it stays out of the shell history.
key.saved: I stored the key in a safe place.
key.close: Close and clear the key from the screen
key.createHint: Single-use key, at most {{max}} minutes, always with an explicit expiry.

owners.tags: Tags only (no owner — shared devices, servers)

key.tagsHint: Only tags declared in the tenant's catalog; a tags-only key needs at least one tag.
key.noTags: The tag catalog is empty — declare tags on the Tag catalog page.
key.reusableHint: One key enrolls several devices until it expires — for automation only.
key.ephemeralHint: The node is removed when it disconnects (containers, CI).
key.secretGone: The key of this submission is no longer held, so it cannot be shown again: revoke the request in the list and create a new key.

keys.intro: Pre-auth keys and device requests of the tenant. Keys are always short-lived and shown once; revoking expires the key at the control plane and reports done only after reading it back.

mine.title: Your requests
mine.allLink: See every request and key of the tenant

paste.title: Paste a link or Auth ID
paste.hint: Ran the command but the link opened in another browser? Paste the link the client printed (…/register/hskey-authreq-…) or the Auth ID here.
paste.label: Link or Auth ID

errors.none: No valid Auth ID found (hskey-authreq- and 24 characters).
errors.several: Several Auth IDs — paste a single link.
errors.other_server: The link belongs to another control plane or tenant — it is not sent to this tenant.

claim.title: Confirm a device
claim.cautionTitle: Confirm only if you just ran the command yourself
claim.caution: Confirming attaches the waiting device to your account. Continue only if YOU just ran tailscale up on your own device in the last few minutes.
claim.cautionNever: If someone sent you this link (e-mail, chat), do not confirm — it may be a trick to put a foreign device on the network.
claim.noPendingSeen: None of your device requests is waiting. If you did not just create one on Add device, do not confirm.
claim.pendingSeveral: You have several waiting requests — the one created in this browser session is used; if this session has several, you will be asked to choose.
claim.pick: You have several waiting requests: choose the one of the device that ran the command
claim.ack: I just ran the command on my own device and want to add it.
claim.verifiedHint: The device is enrolled and verified; the current policy applies at once (no grant ⇒ no access yet).
claim.usedTitle: The link was used or has expired
claim.used: A sign-in link works once and lives 15 minutes. Run tailscale up again to get a new link.
claim.endedNotPending: The control plane no longer has a pending sign-in for this link (the link is old, or the control plane restarted), so the device was not added.
claim.endedUpstream: The tenant's control plane did not complete the registration step (no answer or refused), so this request ended without verifying the device.
claim.endedNext: This request and link cannot be used again — do not reopen the old link or rerun the old command. Create a new request on Add device, then run exactly the new command it shows.
claim.disabledTitle: The tenant does not accept web-auth
claim.disabled: The tenant turned web-auth enrollment off — use a single-use pre-auth key on Add device.
claim.phishingTitle: Warning: you have no device request waiting
claim.phishing: None of your device requests is waiting in this session, so this link is not confirmed. If you did not run the command yourself, someone is likely trying to make you add their device to the network — this was recorded.
claim.phishingSession: If you did run the command: create a request on Add device in this browser, then run exactly the command it shows.
claim.invalid: The confirmation link is missing or malformed (or was already handled). Open the link the client printed again, or paste it on Add device.
claim.notMemberTitle: The link is not for your tenant
claim.notMember: You are not a member of the tenant in this link (or you are signed in with another account). Nothing was confirmed.
claim.autoRetry: The confirmation will be sent again once, automatically, when the wait is over — no need to click again.

failure.node_mismatch: The enrolled device did not match the request (hostname other than the issued command, wrong user or tags) — it was deleted at once. Run exactly the command shown.
failure.foreign_node: The device already belongs to someone else — it was disabled (expired) and waits for its owner.
failure.auth_id_not_pending: The control plane no longer had the device's pending sign-in (an old link, or the control plane restarted) — the request has ended: create a new request and run its new command.
failure.claim_unfinished: The confirmation did not finish — create a new request.
failure.issue_unfinished: The command/key could not be issued — create a new request.
failure.key_missing: The key is no longer on the control plane.
failure.node_gone: The device enrolled with this key no longer exists.
failure.record_failed: The enrolled device could not be recorded — try again or contact an administrator.

actions.revoking: Revoking — waiting for the control plane to confirm…
actions.revokeNotApplied: Not revoked: the control plane did not answer, so the request and key are unchanged. Try again.

done.approve: Request {{label}} approved — the requester gets the command/key on Add device.
done.revoke: {{label}} revoked — the control plane confirmed the key/code no longer works.

desc.approve: Once approved, the requester gets the command or key (once) in their own Portal session. You cannot approve your own request.
desc.reject: The request ends; the requester must create a new one.
desc.revoke: The issued key/code is disabled at the control plane and read back before reporting done. An enrolled device is not touched — revoke devices on the Devices page.

startConflict.already_started: The command/key of this request was already issued (shown once) — revoke it and create a new request if it was lost.
startConflict.request_expired: The request waited more than 24 hours and expired — create a new one.
startConflict.not_approved: The request is not approved yet.
startConflict.not_requester: Only the member who made the request can get its command/key.
startConflict.other: The request changed — reload the list.

diagnostics.intro: The tenant's control-plane state and a connectivity check between two devices from control-plane data, with the commands to run on the devices.
diagnostics.notObservable: The server cannot observe the real path between two devices (direct or relayed): the conclusion below comes from control-plane data only — run the commands on the devices to confirm.

instance.title: Control-plane state
instance.edgeHint: Derived from the relay probe's DERP check — the same public listener and hostname as the clients' control connection.

policy.none: No policy is recorded as applied.
policy.latestFailed: The latest application failed — Headscale still holds the policy above.

reasons.no_probe: No dedicated probe — the edge state comes from the relay probe on the same hostname.
reasons.not_observable: The server cannot observe it — run the checklist on the devices.
reasons.never_synced: The device register has never been synced.
reasons.never_applied: No policy is recorded as applied.
reasons.stale: The last check result is stale.

connectivity.title: Connectivity check
connectivity.intro: Choose a source device and a target (device or resource), optionally a TCP port. The result comes from control-plane data; the checklist below lists the commands to run on the devices.

form.portInvalid: The port must be a number from 1 to 65535.
form.noDevices: There is no device you can see.

verdictExplain.allowed: Both devices are online, not expired, and the applied policy has a matching grant. A firewall on the target, the client's state or a network on the way can still block it — confirm with a real TCP connection.
verdictExplain.blocked: At least one check failed (see below) — fix it before trying on the devices.
verdictExplain.unknown: The control plane has not enough data to conclude (no applied policy, or principals the evaluator cannot resolve).

result.title: {{source}} → {{target}} : {{port}}
result.unresolved: Principals that could not be evaluated:

checks.policy_grant: The policy has an allowing grant

checkReasons.no_approved_route: no approved route covers this address
checkReasons.router_offline: the router with the route is offline
checkReasons.tailnet_address: a tailnet address — no route needed
checkReasons.stale_inventory: the register is stale — sync it on the Devices page
checkReasons.relay_unhealthy: the relay is failing — a direct path may still work
checkReasons.instance_unhealthy: the instance is failing — existing connections may keep working
checkReasons.never_applied: no policy is recorded as applied
checkReasons.no_applied_policy: no policy is recorded as applied
checkReasons.no_matching_grant: no grant for this source/target pair
checkReasons.port_not_allowed: grants exist, but not for this port
checkReasons.no_tcp_allowed: grants exist, but not for TCP
checkReasons.unreadable_policy: the applied policy could not be read
checkReasons.unsupported_policy: the policy is not in grants form
checkReasons.unresolved_principals: some principals could not be evaluated

commands.title: Checklist to run on the devices
commands.intro: Run them in order on the source device (unless stated otherwise). Only their results show the real path.
commands.macosNote: macOS: the App Store build uses /Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale instead of "tailscale".
commands.mobileNote: iOS/Android have no CLI: open the Tailscale app, check the target is listed and its connection status, then try the service.
commands.pingNote: "tailscale ping" does not test the policy — only a real TCP connection shows whether the policy allows it.

status.title: Peer list
status.expect: The target (or its router) is listed and not "offline". Last column: "direct <ip:port>" = direct path; "relay \"{{code}}\"" = through the tenant's relay; "-"/idle = no traffic in the last 2 minutes (not a failure).

ping.title: Ping over the tailnet
ping.expect: "pong … via <ip>:<port>" = direct; "via DERP({{code}})" = relayed. It only shows the peer is reachable — it does not test the policy.

netcheck.title: NAT/UDP check
netcheck.expect: "UDP: true", the right public IP; the nearest DERP is the tenant's region ({{code}}).

debug_derp.title: Check the tenant's DERP relay
debug_derp.expect: JSON whose "Info" shows a successful DERP connection and a STUN reply with the public IP:port; "Errors" empty (IPv6 errors are expected — the MVP is IPv4 only).

accept_routes.title: Accept subnet routes (Linux)
accept_routes.expect: Linux does not accept subnet routes by default — run it once, then retry the connection.

tcp_connect.title: Real TCP connection to the port
tcp_connect.expect: "succeeded"/"open" (or TcpTestSucceeded : True) = the port is reachable; refused or timed out = policy, firewall or no listening service.

http_probe.title: HTTP request to the web port
http_probe.expect: Prints an HTTP code (200, 301, 401…) = the service answers; a connection error = blocked.

listen_check.title: Is the service listening on the target?
listen_check.expect: A LISTEN line for the port; none ⇒ the service is not running (the control plane cannot see this).
